description: The Shirwal Caves, also written Shriwal, are a Buddhist rock-cut cave group near the village of Shirwal, about 48 km south of Pune on Wikipedia's account. The complex is listed as fifteen excavations: one chaitya, a prayer or shrine hall, and fourteen viharas that served as monastic dwellings. The caves are described as plain and are said to belong to an early phase of Buddhism, though the source gives no specific dates. It is a Buddhist monastic site rather than a Hindu temple.

sources.what_it_supports: Location (~48 km south of Pune), Buddhist, 15 caves (1 chaitya, 14 viharas), plain, early Buddhism, Ahir 2003 reference.

Shirwal Caves are a group of 15 Buddhist caves located in a small village called Shriwal, 48 km south of Pune, India.
One is Chaitya and 14 Caves represent Vihara. All caves are plain belonging to the early phase of Buddhism.
